en: Hoshea king of Israel stops paying tribute to Assyria and sends to Egypt, and the king of Assyria imprisons him.
Assyria besieges Samaria for three years, captures it, and deports Israel to Assyria.
This happened because Israel had worshipped other gods and followed the customs of the nations.
The LORD had warned them through every prophet, “Turn from your evil ways,” but they would not listen.
They kept walking in the sins of Jeroboam until the LORD removed Israel from his presence.
The king of Assyria settles people from Babylon and other lands in the towns of Samaria.
These nations worship the LORD but also serve their own gods.
zh: 以色列王何細亞不再向亞述進貢，又派人去埃及，亞述王就把他囚禁起來。
亞述圍困撒馬利亞三年，攻取了它，把以色列人擄到亞述。
這是因為以色列人敬拜別的神，隨從列國的風俗。
耶和華曾藉眾先知警告他們：「你們要回頭離開惡道」，他們卻不肯聽從。
他們一直行耶羅波安的罪，直到耶和華把以色列從他面前趕出。
亞述王把巴比倫和其他地方的人安置在撒馬利亞的城鎮。
這些民族敬畏耶和華，同時又事奉自己的神。

about.en: The covenant warns of scattering among the nations
about.zh: 約中警告百姓要被分散到萬民中

about.en: Amos warns of exile beyond Damascus
about.zh: 阿摩司警告要被擄到大馬色以外

about.en: Jews and Samaritans have no dealings with each other
about.zh: 猶太人和撒馬利亞人沒有來往

en: Samaria fell about 722 BC after a three-year siege. Shalmaneser V began it; his successor Sargon II claimed the victory.
Sargon II’s inscriptions say he deported 27,290 people from Samaria and resettled the city with people from other lands.
The ruins of Samaria lie at Sebastia, near Nablus. The Samaritans, today a community of under a thousand, still keep their worship on Mount Gerizim.
zh: 撒馬利亞經過三年的圍困，約在公元前722年陷落。圍城的是撒縵以色五世，他的繼任者撒珥根二世則宣稱是他得勝。
撒珥根二世的碑文說，他從撒馬利亞擄走了27290人，又把別地的人遷入城中。
撒馬利亞城的遺址在納布盧斯附近的塞巴斯蒂亞。今天的撒馬利亞人不足一千人，仍在基利心山守他們的敬拜。

en: Hezekiah trusts in the LORD, removes the high places and rebels against the king of Assyria.
Sennacherib king of Assyria captures the fortified cities of Judah and sends an army to Jerusalem.
The Rabshakeh mocks: no god has rescued any land from Assyria, so how could the LORD rescue Jerusalem?
Hezekiah tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth, goes into the LORD’s house, and sends to the prophet Isaiah.
He spreads Sennacherib’s letter before the LORD and prays, “Save us… so that all the kingdoms may know you alone are God.”
Isaiah answers that the king of Assyria will not come into the city or shoot an arrow there.
That night the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh.
zh: 希西家倚靠耶和華，廢去高處，又背叛亞述王。
亞述王西拿基立攻取猶大所有堅固的城，又派大軍到耶路撒冷。
拉伯沙基譏誚說：列國的神沒有一個能救本國脫離亞述，耶和華又怎能救耶路撒冷呢？
希西家撕裂衣服，披上麻布，進了耶和華的殿，又派人去見以賽亞先知。
他把西拿基立的信在耶和華面前展開，禱告說：「求你拯救我們……使天下萬國都知道唯有你是神。」
以賽亞回覆說，亞述王必不得進這城，也不得在這裏射箭。
當夜，耶和華的使者擊殺亞述的軍營，西拿基立就回尼尼微去了。

about.en: Isaiah tells the same events
about.zh: 以賽亞書記載同一件事

about.en: Chronicles tells of Sennacherib’s invasion
about.zh: 歷代志記載西拿基立入侵

about.en: Hezekiah channels the waters of the Gihon into the city
about.zh: 希西家把基訓的水引入城中

en: Sennacherib invaded Judah in 701 BC. His own record on clay prisms says he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem “like a bird in a cage,” but claims no capture.
Stone reliefs of his siege of Lachish, from his palace at Nineveh, are now in the British Museum in London.
Hezekiah’s Tunnel, about 533 m long, brought water from the Gihon spring into Jerusalem; an inscription found in it tells how it was dug.
Babylonian records also report that Sennacherib was murdered by a son, in 681 BC.
zh: 西拿基立在公元前701年入侵猶大。他在泥柱上的記錄說，他把希西家困在耶路撒冷，「像籠中的鳥」，卻沒有說攻下了城。
記錄他圍攻拉吉的石浮雕原在尼尼微的王宮，現存倫敦大英博物館。
希西家水道長約533米，把基訓泉的水引入耶路撒冷；在水道中發現的銘文記述了開鑿的經過。
巴比倫的記錄也記載，西拿基立在公元前681年被他的兒子殺害。

en: Josiah becomes king at eight years old and does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
While the temple is being repaired, Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the Law.
When it is read to him, Josiah tears his clothes and sends to inquire of the LORD.
The prophet Huldah says disaster will come, but Josiah, who humbled himself, will be buried in peace.
The king reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant to keep the LORD’s commands.
He removes the idols and high places, even the altar Jeroboam had built at Bethel.
They keep a Passover like none since the days of the judges.
zh: 約西亞八歲登基，行耶和華眼中看為正的事。
修理聖殿的時候，希勒家大祭司找到了律法書。
約西亞聽了書上的話，就撕裂衣服，派人去求問耶和華。
女先知戶勒大說災禍必要臨到，但約西亞既然自卑，必平平安安歸到墳墓。
王向眾民宣讀這書，並且立約要遵守耶和華的誡命。
他除掉偶像和高處，連耶羅波安在伯特利所築的壇也拆毀了。
他們守逾越節，自士師時代以來沒有守過這樣的逾越節。

about.en: Chronicles tells of Josiah’s reforms and Passover
about.zh: 歷代志記載約西亞的改革和逾越節

about.en: A man of God names Josiah long before his birth
about.zh: 神人在約西亞出生前很久就提到他的名字

about.en: Moses commands that the law be read to all the people
about.zh: 摩西吩咐向眾民宣讀律法

en: Josiah reigned about 640–609 BC; the book was found in his eighteenth year, about 622 BC.
Many scholars identify the book of the Law found in the temple with Deuteronomy, or part of it.
Josiah was killed at Megiddo in 609 BC, when Pharaoh Neco marched north to the Euphrates to join Assyria against Babylon.
zh: 約西亞約在公元前640至609年在位；律法書是在他第十八年，約公元前622年找到的。
許多學者認為，在聖殿裏找到的律法書就是申命記或其中一部分。
公元前609年，法老尼哥北上伯拉河，要與亞述聯手對抗巴比倫，約西亞在米吉多被殺。

en: The word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, a priest’s son from Anathoth, in Josiah’s thirteenth year.
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you… I appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
Jeremiah protests, “I am only a boy,” but the LORD says, “Do not be afraid, for I am with you.”
The LORD touches his mouth: “I have put my words in your mouth.”
He sees an almond branch: the LORD is watching over his word to carry it out.
He sees a boiling pot tipped away from the north: disaster will come from the north.
The LORD makes him a fortified city: “They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you.”
zh: 約西亞第十三年，耶和華的話臨到亞拿突祭司希勒家的兒子耶利米。
「我還沒有在母腹中造你，就已經認識你……我已立你作列國的先知。」
耶利米推辭說：「我只是個孩子。」耶和華卻說：「不要怕，因為我與你同在。」
耶和華摸他的口，說：「我已把我的話放在你口中。」
他看見一根杏樹枝：耶和華留意看守他的話，必使它成就。
他看見一個從北方傾側的燒開的鍋：災禍必從北方來。
耶和華使他成為堅固的城：「他們要攻擊你，卻不能勝過你。」

about.en: Moses says he cannot speak well; God will teach him
about.zh: 摩西推辭說自己拙口，神要指教他

about.en: Isaiah’s call: “Here I am. Send me!”
about.zh: 以賽亞蒙召：「我在這裏，請差遣我！」

about.en: Paul: God set me apart from my mother’s womb
about.zh: 保羅說神從他在母腹中就分別他

about.en: God formed me in my mother’s womb
about.zh: 我在母腹中，神就編織了我

en: Josiah’s thirteenth year was about 627 BC; Jeremiah went on prophesying until after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC.
Anathoth was a town of priests in Benjamin, about 5 km (3 miles) northeast of Jerusalem, near today’s Anata.
In Hebrew, “almond” (shaqed) sounds like “watching” (shoqed). The almond is the first tree in the land to blossom, in late winter.
zh: 約西亞第十三年約是公元前627年；耶利米一直說預言，直到公元前586年耶路撒冷陷落以後。
亞拿突是便雅憫境內祭司的城，在耶路撒冷東北約5公里，靠近今天的阿納塔。
希伯來文「杏樹」（沙克德）和「看守」（索克德）讀音相近。杏樹是這地最早開花的樹，在冬末開花。

title.en: Jeremiah: the potter and the new covenant

en: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the potter’s house, where the potter is working at the wheel.
When a pot is spoiled in his hand, the potter makes it again into another vessel.
“Like the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.”
If a nation turns from its evil, the LORD will relent of the disaster; Judah is called to turn back.
The people answer, “It’s hopeless! We will follow our own plans,” and plot against Jeremiah.
The LORD promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah, not like the covenant they broke.
“I will write it on their hearts… I will forgive their wrongdoing, and I will remember their sin no more.”
zh: 耶和華打發耶利米到陶匠的家裏去，陶匠正在轉輪上做器皿。
器皿在他手中做壞了，陶匠就用那泥另做別的器皿。
「以色列家啊，泥在陶匠手中怎樣，你們在我手中也怎樣。」
邦國若回頭離開惡行，耶和華就改變心意，不降災禍；他呼召猶大回頭。
百姓卻回答：「沒有指望了！我們要照自己的計謀去行。」又設計謀害耶利米。
耶和華應許與以色列家和猶大家另立新約，不像他們所背棄的那約。
「我要把律法寫在他們心上……我要赦免他們的罪孽，不再記念他們的罪。」

about.en: Hebrews quotes the promise of the new covenant
about.zh: 希伯來書引用新約的應許

about.en: Jesus: this cup is the new covenant in my blood
about.zh: 耶穌說這杯是用他的血所立的新約

about.en: Paul: the potter has rights over the clay
about.zh: 保羅論陶匠有權柄支配泥土

about.en: God promises a new heart and a new spirit
about.zh: 神應許賜新心和新靈

en: Clay pots were the everyday containers of the ancient Near East; broken pieces, called potsherds, are the most common find at excavations.
Potters shaped clay on a turning wheel; while the clay was still soft, a spoiled pot could be pressed down and shaped again.
Jeremiah 31:31–34 is the longest Old Testament passage quoted in the New Testament (Hebrews 8:8–12).
zh: 陶器是古代近東日常使用的器皿；陶器碎片是考古發掘中最常見的出土物。
陶匠在轉輪上塑造泥土；泥土還軟的時候，做壞的器皿可以壓扁重做。
耶利米書31章31至34節是新約引用最長的一段舊約經文（希伯來書8章8至12節）。

en: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon besieges Jerusalem until there is no food left in the city.
The wall is broken through; King Zedekiah flees but is captured in the plains of Jericho.
His sons are killed before his eyes; he is blinded and taken to Babylon in bronze shackles.
Nebuzaradan burns the house of the LORD, the palace and every great house, and the walls are torn down.
The people are taken into exile; only some of the poorest are left to work the vineyards and fields.
Years later in Babylon, King Jehoiachin is released from prison and eats at the king’s table.
Lamentations: “Because of the LORD’s faithful love we are not finished… great is your faithfulness.”
zh: 巴比倫王尼布甲尼撒圍困耶路撒冷，直到城中斷了糧。
城牆被攻破；西底家王逃跑，卻在耶利哥平原被擒。
他的兒子們在他眼前被殺；他被剜了眼睛，用銅鏈鎖着帶到巴比倫。
尼布撒拉旦焚燒耶和華的殿、王宮和所有大戶的房屋，又拆毀城牆。
百姓被擄走，只留下一些最窮的人修理葡萄園，耕種田地。
多年以後，在巴比倫，約雅斤王從監牢裏出來，常在王的席上吃飯。
耶利米哀歌：「我們沒有滅絕，是出於耶和華的慈愛……你的信實何其廣大！」

about.en: The land keeps its Sabbaths for seventy years
about.zh: 地享受安息，直滿七十年

about.en: By the rivers of Babylon we wept
about.zh: 我們在巴比倫的河邊哭泣

about.en: After seventy years God will bring them back
about.zh: 七十年滿了，神必領他們回來

en: Jerusalem fell in 586 BC (some date it 587 BC), after a siege of about a year and a half.
Clay ration tablets found in Babylon list oil given to “Jehoiachin, king of Judah,” and his sons.
Lamentations is traditionally ascribed to Jeremiah. Its first four poems are acrostics on the Hebrew alphabet; chapter 3 gives three verses to each letter.
Jews mourn the destruction of the temple on the fast of Tisha B’Av, when Lamentations is read.
zh: 耶路撒冷在公元前586年陷落（也有人定為公元前587年），城被圍困約一年半。
在巴比倫出土的配給泥版，記載了發給「猶大王約雅斤」和他兒子們的油。
耶利米哀歌傳統上認為是耶利米所寫。前四首詩按希伯來字母順序排列；第3章每個字母佔三節。
猶太人在猶太曆阿布月九日禁食，哀悼聖殿被毀，並在這天誦讀耶利米哀歌。

en: Among the exiles by the river Chebar, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s exile, Ezekiel sees visions of God.
He sees living creatures and wheels, and above them a throne with a likeness like a human being, shining like fire.
It is the likeness of the glory of the LORD, and Ezekiel falls on his face.
The LORD sends him to rebellious Israel: whether they listen or not, they will know a prophet has been among them.
He is given a scroll of laments to eat, and in his mouth it is as sweet as honey.
He sits among the exiles at Tel-abib for seven days, overwhelmed.
The LORD makes him a watchman for Israel, to warn the wicked to turn from their way.
zh: 約雅斤王被擄第五年，以西結在迦巴魯河邊被擄的人中，看見了神的異象。
他看見活物和輪子，上面有寶座，寶座上有彷彿人的形像，四圍發出火的光輝。
這是耶和華榮耀的形像；以西結看見，就俯伏在地。
耶和華差他到悖逆的以色列人那裏：他們聽也好，不聽也好，必知道有先知在他們中間。
神給他一卷寫滿哀歌的書卷吃，在他口中甜如蜜。
他在提勒‧亞畢被擄的人中間坐了七天，驚愕不已。
耶和華立他作以色列家的守望者，警告惡人離開惡道。

about.en: John sees four living creatures around the throne
about.zh: 約翰看見寶座周圍的四活物

about.en: John eats a little scroll, sweet as honey
about.zh: 約翰吃下小書卷，口中甜如蜜

about.en: The watchman’s duty, given again
about.zh: 再次講述守望者的責任

en: Ezekiel, a priest, was taken to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC; his call came five years later, about 593 BC.
The Chebar was a canal of the Euphrates near the city of Nippur in southern Iraq; Babylonian documents name it.
Tel-abib probably meant “mound of the flood,” an old ruin mound. The modern city of Tel Aviv took its name from this verse.
zh: 以西結是祭司，公元前597年與約雅斤王一同被擄到巴比倫；五年後，約公元前593年，他蒙召作先知。
迦巴魯河是伯拉河的一條運河，在今伊拉克南部的尼普爾城附近，巴比倫的文獻也提到它。
提勒‧亞畢大概是「洪水丘」的意思，指古老的廢墟土丘。現代城市特拉維夫的名字就是取自這節經文。

en: The Spirit of the LORD sets Ezekiel down in a valley full of very dry bones.
“Son of man, can these bones live?” Ezekiel answers, “Lord GOD, you know.”
He prophesies; the bones rattle together, and sinews, flesh and skin cover them, but there is no breath.
He prophesies to the breath; they come to life and stand on their feet, a very great army.
The bones are the whole house of Israel, who say, “Our hope is gone”; God will open their graves and put his Spirit in them.
Two sticks, for Judah and for Joseph, become one: God will make them one nation with one king.
“My servant David will be king over them,” and God’s sanctuary will be among them forever.
zh: 耶和華的靈把以西結放在一個佈滿枯乾骸骨的平原中。
「人子啊，這些骸骨能復活嗎？」以西結回答：「主耶和華啊，你是知道的。」
他說預言，骸骨就互相連接，有筋、有肉、有皮包住，只是還沒有氣息。
他向氣息說預言，他們就活了，站起來，成為極大的軍隊。
這些骸骨就是以色列全家，他們說：「我們的指望斷絕了」；神要打開他們的墳墓，把他的靈放在他們裏面。
寫着猶大和約瑟的兩根木杖合而為一：神要使他們成為一國，歸一個王。
「我的僕人大衛必作他們的王」，神的聖所必永遠在他們中間。

about.en: God breathes the breath of life into the first man
about.zh: 神將生命的氣息吹進第一個人

about.en: A new heart, and God’s Spirit within
about.zh: 新心，以及神的靈在人裏面

about.en: Born of the Spirit; the wind blows where it wishes
about.zh: 從聖靈生；風隨意而吹

about.en: Jesus breathes on the disciples: “Receive the Holy Spirit”
about.zh: 耶穌向門徒吹氣：「受聖靈」

en: The Hebrew word ruach means breath, wind and spirit; this chapter uses it in all three senses.
The vision came to the exiles in Babylon after Jerusalem fell in 586 BC, when both Israel and Judah had lost their land.
A wall painting of this vision survives from the synagogue at Dura-Europos in Syria, painted in the mid-200s AD.
zh: 希伯來文「魯阿赫」可以指氣息、風和靈；本章三種意思都用到了。
這異象是在公元前586年耶路撒冷陷落以後，賜給在巴比倫被擄的人；那時以色列和猶大都已失去了故土。
敘利亞杜拉歐羅普斯的會堂留有一幅描繪這異象的壁畫，約繪於公元三世紀中葉。

en: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and takes vessels from the house of God to Babylonia.
Young nobles of Judah, among them Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, are chosen to train for the king’s service.
They are given new names: Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.
Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king’s food and wine.
He asks for a ten-day test of vegetables and water; at the end they look healthier than the others.
God gives the four knowledge and wisdom, and Daniel understanding of visions and dreams.
The king finds them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his kingdom.
zh: 尼布甲尼撒圍困耶路撒冷，把神殿中的器皿帶到巴比倫地。
猶大的貴族少年被選出來，學習服侍王，其中有但以理、哈拿尼雅、米沙利和亞撒利雅。
他們被改了名字：伯提沙撒、沙得拉、米煞和亞伯尼歌。
但以理立志不用王的食物和酒玷污自己。
他請求用蔬菜和清水試驗十天；十天後，他們比其他少年更健康。
神賜這四個少年知識和智慧，又使但以理明白各樣的異象和夢。
王發現他們比全國所有的術士和巫師勝過十倍。

about.en: Jehoiakim becomes Nebuchadnezzar’s servant
about.zh: 約雅敬臣服於尼布甲尼撒

about.en: The law on clean and unclean food
about.zh: 律法中潔淨與不潔淨的食物

about.en: Daniel and his friends promoted after the king’s dream
about.zh: 王的夢以後，但以理和三友被提拔

en: Nebuchadnezzar’s first campaign against Jerusalem is usually dated 605 BC, the year he became king of Babylon.
Babylon stood on the Euphrates River about 85 km (55 miles) south of Baghdad, Iraq.
Daniel 2:4 to 7:28 is written in Aramaic, the common language of the empire; the rest of the book is in Hebrew.
zh: 尼布甲尼撒第一次攻打耶路撒冷，一般定在公元前605年，就是他作巴比倫王的那一年。
巴比倫城位於伯拉河畔，在今伊拉克巴格達以南約85公里。
但以理書2章4節至7章28節是用亞蘭文寫的，亞蘭文是當時帝國通用的語言；其餘部分是希伯來文。

en: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a gold statue sixty cubits high on the plain of Dura.
All must fall down and worship it when the music sounds, or be thrown into a blazing furnace.
Some Chaldeans report that Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego do not serve the king’s gods or worship the statue.
They answer, “Our God is able to rescue us… But even if he does not… we will not serve your gods.”
The furnace is heated seven times hotter, and the three are thrown in, tied up.
The king sees four men walking unharmed in the fire, the fourth like a son of the gods.
They come out without even the smell of fire on them, and the king blesses their God.
zh: 尼布甲尼撒在杜拉平原立了一個高六十肘的金像。
眾人一聽見樂聲，就要俯伏敬拜金像，否則要被扔進烈火的窯中。
有幾個迦勒底人控告沙得拉、米煞和亞伯尼歌，不事奉王的神，也不拜金像。
他們回答：「我們的神能救我們……即或不然……我們也決不事奉你的神。」
王命人把窯燒熱，比平常熱七倍，把三人捆起來扔進窯裏。
王看見有四個人在火中行走，毫無損傷，第四個的相貌好像神子。
他們從火中出來，身上連火燎的氣味也沒有，王就稱頌他們的神。

about.en: No other gods; do not bow down to images
about.zh: 不可有別的神，不可跪拜偶像

about.en: When you walk through fire, you will not be burned
about.zh: 你從火中行走，必不被燒傷

about.en: By faith some quenched the power of fire
about.zh: 有人藉着信撲滅了烈火的威力

en: A cubit was about 45 cm (18 in), so the statue was about 27 m (90 ft) high and 2.7 m wide.
Babylonian mathematics counted in sixties; we still divide an hour into sixty minutes because of it.
The site of the plain of Dura is not known for certain; several places in Babylonia bore the name.
zh: 一肘約45厘米，所以金像約高27米，寬2.7米。
巴比倫的數學以六十進位；今天一小時分為六十分鐘，就是源於此。
杜拉平原的確切位置不詳；巴比倫有好幾個地方都叫這個名字。

en: King Belshazzar holds a great feast and drinks from the gold vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem.
They praise the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.
The fingers of a human hand appear and write on the palace wall, and the king turns pale.
None of the wise men can read it; the queen tells the king to call Daniel.
Daniel reminds him how God humbled Nebuchadnezzar, yet Belshazzar has not humbled his heart.
Mene: God has numbered your kingdom. Tekel: you are weighed and found lacking. Peres: your kingdom goes to the Medes and Persians.
That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king is killed.
zh: 伯沙撒王大擺筵席，用從耶路撒冷聖殿帶來的金器喝酒。
他們讚美金、銀、銅、鐵、木、石所造的神。
忽然有人的指頭出現，在王宮的牆上寫字，王就臉色大變。
智慧人都不能讀出那文字；王后請王召但以理來。
但以理提醒王，神怎樣使尼布甲尼撒降卑，伯沙撒卻沒有自卑。
彌尼：神已數算你的國；提客勒：你被稱在天平上，顯出不足；毗勒斯：你的國要歸給米底亞人和波斯人。
當夜，迦勒底王伯沙撒被殺。

about.en: The LORD stirs up the kings of the Medes against Babylon
about.zh: 耶和華激動米底亞君王攻擊巴比倫

about.en: Cyrus, the LORD’s anointed
about.zh: 耶和華的受膏者古列

about.en: Pride goes before destruction
about.zh: 驕傲走在毀滅之前

en: Babylon fell to Cyrus of Persia in 539 BC, as Babylonian chronicles and the Cyrus Cylinder record.
Babylonian texts name Belshazzar as son of King Nabonidus, ruling in Babylon while his father stayed in Arabia; this is often taken to explain “third in the kingdom.”
Mene, tekel and peres are Aramaic words that also name weights: the mina, the shekel and the half-mina.
zh: 公元前539年，巴比倫被波斯王古列攻陷，巴比倫的編年史和古列圓柱都有記載。
巴比倫的文獻記載伯沙撒是拿波尼度王的兒子，在父親留居阿拉伯期間治理巴比倫；許多人以此解釋「位列第三」的意思。
彌尼、提客勒、毗勒斯是亞蘭文，也是重量單位的名稱：彌那、舍客勒和半彌那。

en: Darius the Mede makes Daniel one of three chief officials and plans to set him over the whole kingdom.
The other officials find no fault in him, so they persuade the king to ban requests to anyone but the king for thirty days.
Daniel still prays three times a day at windows open toward Jerusalem, as he had done before.
The king is distressed, but the law of the Medes and Persians cannot be changed; Daniel is thrown into the lions’ pit.
At dawn the king calls, and Daniel answers, “My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths.”
Daniel is lifted out unharmed, because he trusted in his God; his accusers are thrown in.
Darius decrees that all must fear the God of Daniel, the living God, whose kingdom will never be destroyed.
zh: 米底亞人大利烏立但以理為三位總長之一，並打算立他治理全國。
其他官員找不到他的錯處，就勸王下禁令：三十天內，除了向王以外，不可向任何神或人祈求。
但以理仍像往常一樣，一日三次在開向耶路撒冷的窗前禱告。
王十分憂愁，但米底亞和波斯的律例不能更改；但以理就被扔進獅子坑。
天一亮，王呼叫但以理；但以理回答：「我的神差遣使者封住了獅子的口。」
但以理從坑裏被拉上來，毫無損傷，因為他信靠他的神；控告他的人卻被扔進坑中。
大利烏下詔，要人人敬畏但以理的神，他是永活的神，他的國永不敗壞。

about.en: Solomon prays for exiles who pray toward the city
about.zh: 所羅門為向聖城禱告的被擄者祈求

about.en: Evening, morning and noon I cry out
about.zh: 晚上、早晨、中午我都要哀訴

about.en: A decree sealed with the king’s ring cannot be revoked
about.zh: 用王的戒指蓋印的詔書不能收回

about.en: By faith some shut the mouths of lions
about.zh: 有人藉着信堵住了獅子的口

en: “Darius the Mede” is known only from Daniel. Scholars differ on who he was; some identify him with Cyrus, others with Gubaru, a governor of Babylon.
Kings of the region kept lions; Assyrian palace reliefs show royal lion hunts, and Babylon’s processional way was lined with glazed-brick lions.
Praying toward Jerusalem follows Solomon’s prayer (1 Kings 8:48). A tomb at Susa, in Iran, is traditionally Daniel’s.
In this site’s Bible, Daniel 6 follows the Aramaic numbering: English 6:1–28 is 6:2–29 here.
zh: 「米底亞人大利烏」只見於但以理書。學者對他是誰看法不一，有人認為就是古列，也有人認為是巴比倫總督古巴魯。
這一帶的君王常飼養獅子；亞述王宮的浮雕刻有君王獵獅的場面，巴比倫的遊行大道兩旁飾有琉璃磚獅子。
向耶路撒冷禱告是照着所羅門的禱告（列王紀上8章48節）。伊朗書珊的一座墳墓相傳是但以理的墓。
本站聖經依照亞蘭文的節數：英文但以理書6章1至28節在這裏是6章2至29節。
